base.description: The SHA-256 of the base the glb was made from.
The SHA-256 of the file kept as the base, which the XML was exported from.

extension.description: The game extension the cooked file has.

Credit.description: Who made an asset, where it was found and on what terms it may be used: what a credits file says of it.

licence.description: The terms it may be used on: the name of a licence such as `CC-BY-4.0`, or a sentence.

url.description: Where it was found: a page, a shop, or the pack it was taken from.

Origin.description: Where an asset's content came from.

cooked_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of what the cook of this source made when the game's file was imported, which a build takes for the game's file as `sha256` is, because a cook writes OpenRage's form of a file and not the game's bytes.

from_game.description: True when the content is the game's, which a build leaves out while it is still the game's file and a repository does not keep by default.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the compiled original, to tell that the game's file changed after an update.

description: The contents of `asset.json`; nothing in it changes when the payload does.

compile.description: What a kind that compiles from a base keeps in the manifest: a model the mode and the hash of the base its glb was made from, a metadata source the extension of the file and the hash of the base its XML was exported from

credit.description: Who made the asset and on what terms it may be used, which a build can list in a credits file; nothing compiles from it.

id.description: Made once and never changed, so a rename or a move breaks no reference to the asset.

kind.description: A word with no platform letter that chooses the compiler, such as `textures`.

name.description: One plain file name: the folder is `<name>.<kind>.src` and the cook writes `<name>.ytd`.

target.description: The slug of the RSC7 layout the asset compiles to, such as `gen8`.

title: asset.json
